column12:
One of my most unforgettable memories from my MS research in 2008 was travelling from place to place, searching for insects for my enzymatic research. Finding enough samples was extremely difficult, which frustrated me deeply. During that challenging period, Dr. Dwaipayan Shikdar and my other respected professors continuously encouraged me.
After I finally collected the larvae. I reared them in the laboratory and watched them transform into beautiful butterflies. Seeing that transformation with my own eyes was truly amazing—one of those rare moments when scientific research becomes a beautiful life experience.
Actually, research is not only about experiments and results; it is about patience, persistence, and curiosity. Those butterflies remind me of the beautiful beginning of my scientific journey.

“গুরু যদি এক বর্ণ শিষ্যের শিখায় কোনদিন, পৃথিবীতে নেই দ্রব্য যা দিয়ে শোধ দিবে ঋণ।”
When Professor Dr. Dwaipayan Sikder Sir accepted me as his thesis student, my life took an unexpected turn. His words still inspire me: “Work hard, stay committed, and you can change your life.”
Opening the Window to Research 
While many of our classmates conducted their thesis research at renowned institutions such as ICDDR,B, BIRDEM, the University of Dhaka, and BCSIR, Suman and I began our research journey in a completely different setting. We started working in a long-abandoned departmental laboratory that had remained locked for years and was used only occasionally for undergraduate practical classes.
With determination and perseverance, we spent two to three weeks transforming the space—sweeping, scrubbing, cleaning, and clearing away rodents and accumulated spider webs. Despite having limited resources and only a few traditional instruments, we planted our vision and opened a window of dreams beneath the old Marine Science Building.
Rather than discouraging us, these limitations strengthened our resilience and inspired us to find creative solutions with the resources we had. In many ways, our efforts marked the beginning of the department’s first chapter of student-led thesis research.
Memorable Sample Collections
Suman and I spent weeks living among farmers in Chakaria and Lama, Bandarban, collecting insect-infested brinjal directly from the fields and transporting nearly 80–100 kilograms of samples back to our laboratory.
One journey remains unforgettable: traveling by a small boat from Manikpur to Lama for sample collection under the glow of a full moon. Accompanied by my wife and our batchmate Dipa Das, what began as a research expedition became a cherished memory from the early days of my married life.
My Mentor Is My Real Hero — A Personal Tribute
When I look back at my journey, I realize that one person quietly changed the course of my life—my mentor, Professor Dr. Dwaipayan Sikder Sir.
He spent countless hours in our modest laboratory, patiently guiding us, correcting our mistakes, and encouraging us to dream bigger. Even when away, he would call late at night to ask about our progress; during holidays, he welcomed us into his home, turning his time into lessons of knowledge, reflection, and hope.
When I joined his research team, our laboratory had little more than aging instruments and limited resources. Yet Sir taught us not to focus on what we lacked, but on what we could create. Under his vision and unwavering faith in us, that humble laboratory became a place of discovery, resilience, and dreams.
To me, Sir is not simply a mentor—he is my true hero. His patience, compassion, and ideals shaped not only my academic journey but also the person I became. His words remain forever etched in my heart:
“Teachers live on through the thoughts and ideals of their students.”
And I carry one enduring conviction: wherever my journey takes me, a part of my Guru will always live on through me.
Dear Suman—your kindness and unwavering support have shaped my journey in ways beyond words. Grateful to you, always—perhaps some bonds are written across lifetimes.
